intended_object: The conjugate of a map τ : ℤ → ℤ by the negation involution n ↦ −n, i.e. the function n ↦ −τ(−n). In Pflueger's setting this is the reflection of an affine permutation, used to define the transmission permutation after swapping the two marks. This comes from the docstring, the name and how the library uses it (swapTransmissionPermutation, IsKAffine preservation, kInversionCount invariance).
explanation: The body `fun n => -τ (-n)` is exactly ι ∘ τ ∘ ι with ι(n) = −n, and ι is its own inverse. So it is precisely conjugation by negation, as the docstring says. There are no degenerate cases to worry about. The operation would make sense on any additive group. Here, though, it is part of a vocabulary of functions ℤ → ℤ (affine permutations, inversions, quadrant sets) that only exists over ℤ, so working on ℤ is the natural setting for this library. Mathlib has no dedicated named definition for "conjugation by negation" of an endofunction. A related construction is conjugation in `Equiv.Perm` by `Equiv.neg`, but that applies to bijections, while this definition takes raw functions. The definition is correct and suited to its context.
